Q: Git: pull request from the fork of a fork back to the original upstream repo A:

For the command line just point git at the right remote for the original and merge to the branch (PRs are not required on the CLI for git)

For the github CLI workflow see the Github documentation you specify the target base with the typical fork format user/repo:branch-to-merge-to and your head with my-branch-to-merge-in

that should get you started

Q: How can I recover a MySQL database from a failed Windows SSD if I can’t access phpMyAdmin? A:

Yes, recovery is still possible even if Windows won’t boot. Since you already copied the WAMP folder, check the old MySQL data directory for files like ibdata1, .ibd, and .frm. Those contain the actual database data. Usually you can install the same MySQL/MariaDB version on the new system and copy the old data files into the new data directory, then start MySQL again.

If the database does not show up, it’s often because of version mismatch or InnoDB recovery issues from the SSD failure. In some cases starting MySQL with innodb_force_recovery helps you dump the tables first. If the .ibd files are damaged or MySQL refuses to load them, Try some third pary tools like Stellar Repair for MySQL or Cigati Solutions can sometimes recover the tables and export the data.

Q: Python Selenium accessing HTML source A:

Use:

from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from selenium import webdriver

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
html_source_code = driver.execute_script("return document.body.innerHTML;")
html_soup: BeautifulSoup = BeautifulSoup(html_source_code, 'html.parser')

Now you can apply Beautiful Soup functions to extract data...

Q: Why can't partitions fill backwards? A:

IIUC what you are saying and ignore the morality of the idea (e.g. ignore if the idea is good/bad), then I ask: What do you do when the drive is full? namely how would either OS (Windows or Linux etc.) be expected to know when the drive is full? are the partitions already fixed? If so then how does the location of fixed free space help? If they are not fixed and should be able to consolidate, then the typical implementation (e.g. fill forward) doesn't currently look for the reverse address partition (e.g. block metadata and partition metadata parts needed to make sense of it's boundaries) if unchanged.

Or did I miss something?

(and does windows boot natively on ext4 now? or are the partitions different formats?)

It would also help to see an example of an "easy" implementation (just pseudocode is fine)
